report.headline: Usage projected to shrink to 13.8% in the NBA, well below league norms, while the shooting-efficiency projection carries no real signal.

projection.text: Usage rate is projected at 13.8% in the NBA, down from 16.9% in the G League, with an 80% interval of 8.5% to 19.0% and a 95% interval of 5.7% to 21.8%, against an NBA average of 20.0% (SD 5.3%).

risks.text: Projected usage of 13.8% is a clear drop from the 16.9% share held in the G League and sits well below the NBA's 20.0% average (SD 5.3%).
The 80% prediction interval for usage spans 8.5% to 19.0%, roughly two standard deviations of the NBA distribution, so the model can rank players but not pin down an individual role.
The true shooting projection ties the trivial league-average baseline on error (4.7% vs 4.7%), meaning it should not be used to judge likely shooting efficiency.
The estimate is built on only 45 historical G League to NBA transitions, a thin cohort.

strengths.text: Produced 15.2 points, 2.2 assists, and 5.1 rebounds per 75 possessions in the source G League season.
Shot efficiently in the G League, posting a 61.6% true shooting percentage that stood 1.10 SD above that league's average.
Combined a low 9.4% turnover rate with a 9.7% assist rate.
Belongs to a pool of movers who, conditional on making the move, already sat about 0.27 SD above their own league's average.

uncertainty.text: The true shooting percentage projection of 53.7% is not trustworthy: its 4.7% out-of-fold error is no better than simply guessing the league average, so it carries no information about likely shooting efficiency.
